kubejs.ponder.as_grow.header: Catalyzing Mushroom growth via Block Filling
kubejs.ponder.as_grow.text_1: Block Filling can catalyze the growth of certain mushrooms
kubejs.ponder.as_grow.text_10: Example: A stem block with 6 stems and only 1 cap surrounding...
kubejs.ponder.as_grow.text_11: ...has a 50%% chance to become a cap
kubejs.ponder.as_grow.text_12: Every block in the 3*3*3 area grows. Thus, the final pattern is determined by the initial 5*5*5 area state
kubejs.ponder.as_grow.text_2: If you fill the specified medium block, the mushroom in the 3*3*3 area centered 3 blocks below the medium will grow
kubejs.ponder.as_grow.text_3: Each block's next state is determined by the 3*3*3 area surrounding it
kubejs.ponder.as_grow.text_4: If a block is air and has 6 to 12 mushroom around it, it becomes a mushroom.
kubejs.ponder.as_grow.text_5: Example: A air block with 6 mushrooms surrounding it...
kubejs.ponder.as_grow.text_6: ...will become a mushroom. It has a 75%% chance to become a stem if there are more stems, or a 75%% chance to become a cap if there are more caps
kubejs.ponder.as_grow.text_7: If a block is already a mushroom...
kubejs.ponder.as_grow.text_8: It will die if there are fewer than 3 or more than 8 mushrooms surrounding it
kubejs.ponder.as_grow.text_9: Otherwise, it has 50%% chance to change its form (between stem and cap) to approach the ideal ratio of cap to stem. For red mushrooms, this value is 6

kubejs.ponder.belt_mixing.text_2: To control the sequence of items, you can use methods like these:
kubejs.ponder.belt_mixing.text_3: Use Brass Funnels to regulate input quantities.

kubejs.ponder.belt_mixing.text_6: ...and use Clutches to control the flow!
kubejs.ponder.belt_mixing.text_7: Don't limit yourself to the examples shown here — experiment and find your own solutions!

kubejs.ponder.covariant_reactor_fuel_and: Using the Reactor Fuel Rod and Control Rod
Similar to a Steam Generator, you can freely design the structure of the Covariant Reactor and directly control its operational efficiency!
Place Reactor Fuel Rods within a 3*1*3 area around the Covariant Reactor to make it operational
As the number of Fuel Rods increases, power generation and heat production will rise exponentially!
At the start of each reaction, the Fuel Rods will be turned into brass blocks (if there is only one fuel rod, it will not be turned into a brass block)
If you don't want to consume too many Fuel Rods, you can place Control Rods within the range!
Each Control Rod reduces the Fuel Rod consumption probability by 12.5%%!
Additionally, if the core's internal power is overflow, the generated Covariant Heat will be doubled!
kubejs.ponder.covariant_reactor_heat.tex: If the Covariant Heat in the reactor exceeds 1,474,560 mB, the reactor will overheat and explode! This is why you need to cool it down!
You can flexibly switch the reactor's state by pistons, sticky pistons or contraptions
However, it's important to note that once a reactor's reaction begins, it cannot be ended prematurely, so you must move the Control Rods and Fuel Rods in advance!
To cooldown, first, remove the Fuel Rods from around the reactor...
...then, place at least four Control Rods, and the reactor will enter cooling mode
You have two cooling options to choose:
The first option, pumping in Cryogen within the range
The reactor will cool down every 5 ticks, converting up to 4B of Cryogen into Overheated Steam each time
The second option, supplying Radiators into the controller
The reactor will cool down every 40 ticks, consuming 6 Radiator each time...
...and then store the generated Overheated Steam in the controller!
kubejs.ponder.covariant_reactor_io.text_: The reactor has certain automatic input and output capabilities!
First, it automatically draws power from above and distributes it to the surroundings
Secondly, it automatically extracts Radiators from containers placed above
Finally, it automatically outputs internal Overheated Steam upwards!

kubejs.ponder.matrix_2.text_1: Information Elements are a unique type of substance that conveys information through their distinct spatial structures
kubejs.ponder.matrix_2.text_16: Matrix elements can be of any type, but for Information Elements, only numbers are used to represent their structure
kubejs.ponder.matrix_2.text_17: For Information Elements, the first three phases have specific roles
kubejs.ponder.matrix_2.text_18: R phase determines its red tendency
kubejs.ponder.matrix_2.text_19: G phase determines its green tendency
kubejs.ponder.matrix_2.text_2: The spatial structure of a Information Element can be divided into several phases, each represented by a 2*2 matrix
kubejs.ponder.matrix_2.text_20: B phase determines its blue tendency
kubejs.ponder.matrix_2.text_21: The remaining phases have no individual names
kubejs.ponder.matrix_2.text_7: A matrix is a rectangular array of elements arranged in m rows and n columns
kubejs.ponder.matrix_2.text_9: Elements are located by their row (i) and column (j)
kubejs.ponder.matrix_addition.text_1: First, let's look at matrix addition, using A + B = C as an example:
kubejs.ponder.matrix_addition.text_4: To add matrices, Matrix A and Matrix B must have the same size (rows and columns).
kubejs.ponder.matrix_addition.text_7: To perform addition, add each corresponding pair of elements from A and B to get the elements of C!

kubejs.ponder.matrix_multiplication.head: Matrix Multiplication
kubejs.ponder.matrix_multiplication.text: Now, let's look at matrix multiplication, using A · B = C as an example:
This gives the element at row i, column j of matrix C
To multiply two matrices, the number of columns in A must equal the number of rows in B
To perform multiplication, multiply the elements in the i-th row of A with the elements in the j-th column of B in sequence, then sum them (i.e. dot product of A[i][] and B[][j])

kubejs.ponder.matrix_transposition.heade: Information Element Processing - Transposition and Anti-Transposition
kubejs.ponder.matrix_transposition.text_: You can use Block Filling to perform transposition or anti-transposition on Information Elements placed on a Depot
The output Depot must be empty
The direction of the Placard determines the input and output directions
Slime Crystal must be present on the Placard
Using Ethanol on Red Mushroom Blocks will yield the transposition of the initial Information Element
Using Ethanol on Brown Mushroom Blocks will yield the anti-transposition (transposition on anti-diagonal) of the initial Information Element
After processing, the Information Element will be output to the Depot

kubejs.ponder.reaping_machine.text_5: Stem Reaper consumes appropriate fluid to automatically harvest the mushroom stem blocks above it
kubejs.ponder.reaping_machine.text_6: You can only input the required fluid from below
kubejs.ponder.reaping_machine.text_7: Additionally, Reapers will break if an incorrect block type appears above them!
kubejs.ponder.recive_airdrop.text_1: After flight, the Airdrop will appear at the highest Y of the same coordinates (X, Z) on the target planet and descend
kubejs.ponder.recive_airdrop.text_2: You can simply use a 3*3 array of Depots to receive the Airdrop
kubejs.ponder.recive_airdrop.text_3: After unloading, the contents of the Airdrop will be distributed to the eight surrounding Depots
kubejs.ponder.recive_elevator.text_1: After flight, the Space Elevator will drop a Airdrop at the same coordinates (X, Z) on the target orbit and return
kubejs.ponder.recive_elevator.text_2: Unlike Carriers Rockets and Orbit Airdrop Cannons, you should use a 3*3 array of Item Vaults to receive it
kubejs.ponder.recive_elevator.text_3: After unloading, the contents of the Airdrop will be sent to the Item Vaults below
kubejs.ponder.recive_elevator.text_4: If no Item Vaults are present, the Airdrop will directly replace the block below!
kubejs.ponder.recive_rocket.text_1: After flight, the Rocket will appear at the highest Y of the same coordinates (X, Z) on the target planet and descend
kubejs.ponder.recive_rocket.text_2: You can simply use a 3*3 array of Depots to receive the Rocket
kubejs.ponder.recive_rocket.text_3: After unloading, the contents of the Rocket will be distributed to the eight surrounding Depots
kubejs.ponder.red_mushroom_block.header: Transforming Red Mushroom using Nitrogen Fertilizer via Block Filling
kubejs.ponder.red_mushroom_block.text_2: Transformation results: Red Mushroom Block, Mushroom Stem
kubejs.ponder.red_mushroom_conway.header: Catalyzing Red Mushroom growth via Block Filling
kubejs.ponder.red_mushroom_conway.text_2: Fluid consumption: 250 mB Red Mushroom Spores
kubejs.ponder.rose_quartz.header: Transforming Amethyst Cluster to Rose Quartz using Ethanol via Block Filling
kubejs.ponder.rose_quartz.text_2:
An empty Depot is required
Item output: 1x Rose Quartz
kubejs.ponder.sequenced_assembly.text_1: Sequenced Assembly is an important processing method
kubejs.ponder.sequenced_assembly.text_10: Using a rotating platform doesn't make the line more efficient...
kubejs.ponder.sequenced_assembly.text_11: ...but it does look a lot cooler ewe
kubejs.ponder.sequenced_assembly.text_2: It processes a base item through a defined sequence of steps — such as deploying, pressing, or cutting — to create the final product
kubejs.ponder.sequenced_assembly.text_3: Here is a Sequenced Assembly line for producing Bearings
kubejs.ponder.sequenced_assembly.text_4: It includes most of the components you'll need for a Sequenced Assembly line:
kubejs.ponder.sequenced_assembly.text_6: An output that filters the finished product
kubejs.ponder.sequenced_assembly.text_7: A rotating platform for cyclic assembly (you can also use a looping Mechanical Belt or a Weighted Ejector to achieve the cycle)
kubejs.ponder.sequenced_assembly.text_8: A detection device to control the platform rotation
kubejs.ponder.sequenced_assembly.text_9: And a waste filter (not shown here, but often useful)
kubejs.ponder.set_elevator.text_1: This is an assembled Space Elevator (due to some technical issues, you might not see its cable)
kubejs.ponder.set_elevator.text_2: Before use, you should first ensure that the corresponding coordinates on the orbit have a receiving Item Vaults or platform placed
kubejs.ponder.set_elevator.text_3: You can input the items to be transported into the Item Vaults at the base through various ways
kubejs.ponder.set_elevator.text_4: After providing the controller with the Space Elevator, computational data (via Brass Data Disks), and sufficient power...
kubejs.ponder.set_elevator.text_5: ...simply provide a redstone signal to the controller to launch!
kubejs.ponder.set_elevator.text_6: Note that the machine only accepts Strongly Charging!
kubejs.ponder.set_elevator.text_7: During takeoff, the elevator will load all items from the Item Vaults
kubejs.ponder.set_elevator.text_8: Launching only consumes 1 point of durability from the Space Elevator, which you can easily repair!
kubejs.ponder.set_elevator.text_9: The controller can automatically pull power and items from adjacent containers — this should provide you some convenience!
kubejs.ponder.shaft_furnace.text_1: The Shaft Furnace is a multiblock machine with specific structural requirements
kubejs.ponder.shaft_furnace.text_2: Due to its large structure, it is generally recommended to use Schematicannons for construction rather than manual building
kubejs.ponder.shaft_furnace.text_22: Important: the controller must face the Fluid Tank
kubejs.ponder.shaft_furnace.text_3: If you want to build it manually, here is a simple guide:
kubejs.ponder.sprinkler.text_1: Contrary to what you might think, Sprinklers are not for hydrating farmland
kubejs.ponder.sprinkler.text_2: They use Bonemeal Diluent to boost the growth of nearby crops!
kubejs.ponder.sprinkler.text_3: First, connect pipes and supply them with Bonemeal Diluent
kubejs.ponder.sprinkler.text_4: When operating, the Sprinkler will first absorb 1000 mB of Bonemeal Diluent to start
kubejs.ponder.sprinkler.text_5: Every four seconds, it will consume 500 mB of Bonemeal Diluent, increasing the growth stage of all crops within a 5*1*5 area around by +1
kubejs.ponder.sprinkler.text_6: Important: The Sprinkler does not stop automatically — it will keep running forever!
kubejs.ponder.stone.header: Transforming rocks using Lava via Block Filling
kubejs.ponder.stone.text_2: Transformation results: Andesite, Granite, Diorite, Crimsite
kubejs.ponder.strophar_conway.header: Catalyzing Strophar Mushroom growth via Block Filling
kubejs.ponder.use_airdrop_station.header: Using the Orbit Airdrop Cannon to Launch Airdrops
kubejs.ponder.use_airdrop_station.text_1: The Orbit Airdrop Cannon is used to quickly transfer items from orbit to the ground
kubejs.ponder.use_airdrop_station.text_2: Load the items to be launched into the controller
kubejs.ponder.use_airdrop_station.text_3: You can use a Threshold Switch to read the inventory of the Airdrop Cannon...
kubejs.ponder.use_airdrop_station.text_4: Then, simply provide a redstone signal to launch the Airdrop!
kubejs.ponder.use_airdrop_station.text_5: Note that the machine only accepts Strongly Charging!
kubejs.ponder.use_alloy_furnace.text_1: Various alloys are important industrial materials. You can produce them more efficiently using the Alloy Furnace
kubejs.ponder.use_alloy_furnace.text_2: First, ensure the Alloy Furnace structure is complete and all its Andesite Floodlights are lit
kubejs.ponder.use_alloy_furnace.text_4: Important: The controller must face forward! Most multiblock controllers are directional!
kubejs.ponder.use_alloy_furnace.text_5: Next, activate all the Blaze Burners equipped with Straws (must be in standard "Heated" mode)
kubejs.ponder.use_alloy_furnace.text_6: Then, simply input the required items and wait for the recipe to finish
kubejs.ponder.use_alloy_furnace.text_7: Item outputs remain in the controller for to extraction, while fluid outputs will be discharged to the 3x1x6 area at the back side
kubejs.ponder.use_alloy_furnace.text_8: You can freely build various structures next to the fluid pool to achieve automation. All Andesite Funnels can be replaced with Brass Funnels!
kubejs.ponder.use_anti_warden_bomb.text_: Anti-Warden Bombs are used to quickly clear dangerous elements in Ancient Cities!
Sculk Shriekers and their annoying Darkness effect
Place a container with 4B of water above it...
The bomb will clear all Sculk Shriekers in a 47*13*47 area centered on it...
...all Wardens within a radius of 64 blocks...
...and the Darkness effect on players within a radius of 64 blocks!
kubejs.ponder.use_blasting_compressor.te: The Blasting Compressor can compress metal blocks into plates, or provide a high-temperature, high-pressure environment
First, build the correct multiblock structure around the controller
Important: The controller must face the Container!
Next, provide 256 RPM of rotational speed. All Shafts can be encased!
Then, use Deployers or other means to place input materials in the designated positions
If you're worried about explosions, you can use water to protect the machine!
Finally, ignite the required TNT within the red area!
kubejs.ponder.use_blueprint_builder.head: Using the Blueprint Construction Station
kubejs.ponder.use_blueprint_builder.text: The Blueprint Construction Station is a multiblock machine that requires a specific setup, allowing you to conveniently obtain the schematic materials for constructing other multiblocks!
First, ensure the structure is built correctly...
Important: The controller must face forward!
...Then, provide 64 RPM of rotational speed. The controller only accepts stress from the Gearbox below
...Additionally, you need to fill the machine's frame with 392 (7*8*7) Sand for shaping
After inputting items, setting filters, inserting a Hard Disk, and providing a Barrel, the machine will start the recipe
Once complete, it will output a Barrel containing the required materials for the target multiblock machine
kubejs.ponder.use_condenser.text_1: Use a Atmospheric Condenser to extract vital industrial materials from the air
kubejs.ponder.use_condenser.text_2: First, the Atmospheric Condenser must be built in an area with an atmosphere, such as the Overworld and the Nether
kubejs.ponder.use_condenser.text_4: Important: The controller must face forward!
kubejs.ponder.use_condenser.text_5: Next, input Cryogen via these Smart Fluid Pipes
kubejs.ponder.use_condenser.text_6: Finally, make the Compressor operating in "Pressurizing" mode at 256 RPM counterclockwise
kubejs.ponder.use_condenser.text_7: ...by doing so, the Atmospheric Condenser will produce liquefied gases at its back side
kubejs.ponder.use_condenser.text_8: You can automate by placing pipes above the fluid pool to collect the liquids
kubejs.ponder.use_construction_station.t: The Construction Station is a multiblock machine that accepts up to 4 different items and 4 different fluids as input
First, ensure the structure is built correctly...
...Then, provide 256 RPM of rotational speed. The controller only accepts stress from the Gearbox below
...Additionally, the controller needs power to execute recipes
kubejs.ponder.use_electro_hydro_resonant: Using the Electro Hydro Resonant Tower
The Electro Hydro Resonant Tower can collect and process Electro Hydro from the environment!
First, build the correct multiblock structure around the controller
Lightning is required for the tower to function
You can supply the controller with substantial power to generate its own high-energy lightning bolt...
Or, create sufficient natural lightning nearby to greatly reduce its power consumption!
kubejs.ponder.use_electrolytic_cell.head: Using the Huge Electrolytic Cell
kubejs.ponder.use_electrolytic_cell.text: Frustrated with the low efficiency of regular Electrolyzers? The Huge Electrolytic Cell is your best choice!
...the cathode product will be output from the right side (if there is one)
...the byproduct will be output from the back side (if there is one)
...and the anode product will be output from the left side (if there is one)
If the corresponding electrodes have fluids input/output, the electrode may be consumed when the recipe starts. (Except water electrolysis, check JEI for its probability)
First, build the correct multiblock structure around the controller
Next, supply power to the controller through the accumulator in the structure
The controller will extract suitable raw materials from the corresponding tank in the structure!
Extract the anode reactant on the left side (e.g., O2 in N2 + 2O2 == 2NO2)
Extract the cathode reactant on the right side (e.g., N2 in N2 + 2O2 == 2NO2)
kubejs.ponder.use_huge_crusher.text_1: Frustrated with the low efficiency of Crushing Wheels? The Huge Crusher is your best choice!
kubejs.ponder.use_huge_crusher.text_10: Now, input the required items for the recipe into the green Container...
kubejs.ponder.use_huge_crusher.text_11: ...and collect the output from the red Container
kubejs.ponder.use_huge_crusher.text_12: Additionally, each recipe of the Huge Crusher can run at double efficiency — as long as you can supply materials fast enough!
kubejs.ponder.use_huge_crusher.text_2: First, build the correct multiblock structure around the controller
kubejs.ponder.use_huge_crusher.text_4: Note: you can replace the Container with Drawer Controllers or Drawers...
kubejs.ponder.use_huge_crusher.text_5: ...or simply enlarge them! (but not change their type!)
kubejs.ponder.use_huge_crusher.text_6: Please note the controller must face the stress input!
kubejs.ponder.use_huge_crusher.text_7: Then, provide 256 RPM of rotational speed to the stress input
kubejs.ponder.use_huge_crusher.text_8: To run any recipe, you need to supply Water to the controller at a rate of at least 50 mB/t
kubejs.ponder.use_huge_crusher.text_9: If everything is correct, Structure Fluid will appear inside the controller!
kubejs.ponder.use_hydropress.text_1: The Hydropress is a multiblock machine that requires manual control!
kubejs.ponder.use_hydropress.text_10: Finally, raise the piston back up to generate a new batch of Structure Fluid
kubejs.ponder.use_hydropress.text_2: It can process 9 metal blocks at once, or 1B/3B/6B/9B of molten metal, along with some special recipes!
kubejs.ponder.use_hydropress.text_3: First, build the correct multiblock structure around the controller
kubejs.ponder.use_hydropress.text_4: The controller should face the Brass Funnel
kubejs.ponder.use_hydropress.text_5: You can supply it with any rotational speed you prefer
kubejs.ponder.use_hydropress.text_6: Then, input Water via these Mechanical Pumps
kubejs.ponder.use_hydropress.text_7: The Hydropress can only convert Water into Structure Fluid when the piston is fully raised and everything else is correct
kubejs.ponder.use_hydropress.text_8: Place the input materials at the designated positions using Deployers, Mechanical Pumps, or other means
kubejs.ponder.use_hydropress.text_9: Once Hydraulic Fluid is present, lowering the piston will process the materials (consuming the Structure Fluid)
kubejs.ponder.use_infinity_fetching_pool: Tired of building 512-block fluid pools? The Infinity Fetching Pool is your best choice!
First, build the correct multiblock structure around the controller
Please note that these positions can be replaced with Fluid Tanks, Fluid Drawers, or Drawer Controllers!
Next, provide power to the Accumulators
Then, you need to pour the corresponding fluid in the world at two blocks above the controller (above the center of the large brass boiler)
For available fluid types, please check JEI
kubejs.ponder.use_large_difference_engin: The Large Difference Engine is a high-efficiency computational machine that provides significant computational power
First, ensure the structure is built correctly...
...then, provide 64 RPM of rotational speed. The controller only accepts stress from Encased Chain Drives behind it
kubejs.ponder.use_launcher.text_1: Build a multiblock structure around the controller to complete the Rocket Launch Pad
kubejs.ponder.use_launcher.text_3: If unsure about block types, click the magnifying glass icon to identify them
kubejs.ponder.use_launcher.text_7: Important: The controller must face forward!
kubejs.ponder.use_shaft_furnace.text_1: The Shaft Furnace is a large multiblock machine with unique operational requirements
kubejs.ponder.use_shaft_furnace.text_10: You are free to design your own piping and layout, as long as the multiblock structure remains correct!
kubejs.ponder.use_shaft_furnace.text_11: You can also add various decorations!
kubejs.ponder.use_shaft_furnace.text_3: Important: The controller should face the Fluid Tank!
kubejs.ponder.use_shaft_furnace.text_4: Note: Only the lower 3*6*3 part of the Fluid Tank is actually required!
kubejs.ponder.use_shaft_furnace.text_5: Before any operation, you must first activate all the Blaze Burners in Super-Heated mode
kubejs.ponder.use_shaft_furnace.text_6: Some recipes require Oxygen. Supply it by pumping Oxygen fluid into these two 3*1*1 areas (the structure shown is for demonstration only!)
kubejs.ponder.use_shaft_furnace.text_7: Some recipes require other fluids. Pump them into these two input positions
kubejs.ponder.use_shaft_furnace.text_8: The Funnels around the controller can be freely adjusted for item input and output
kubejs.ponder.use_shaft_furnace.text_9: To output fluid products, you must provide sufficient rotational speed here
kubejs.ponder.use_steam_generator.text_1: Unlike most multiblocks, the structure around the Steam Generator can be designed more freely, which directly affects its efficiency
kubejs.ponder.use_steam_generator.text_2: First, the blocks in the frame around the generator cannot be air
kubejs.ponder.use_steam_generator.text_3: Next, input Pressurized Steam within a 3*3 area around the generator, and supply Lube Oil to the generator
kubejs.ponder.use_steam_generator.text_4: When recipe begins, 25 mB of Lube Oil will be consumed, and each block of Pressurized Steam will be converted into Water, providing 540 FE/t of power per block, lasting 60 ticks
kubejs.ponder.use_steam_generator.text_5: However, each Water source presents in the area when the recipe begins will reduce provided power significantly!
kubejs.ponder.use_steam_generator.text_7: The input Lube Oil and output power can be automatically transferred to the block in front of the generator
kubejs.ponder.use_steam_generator.text_8: In other words, a series of Steam Generators can be connected in sequence!
kubejs.ponder.wood_chip_machine.text_1: Automating certain items requires setting up a looping production line
kubejs.ponder.wood_chip_machine.text_2: In a looping production line, items circulate repeatedly, multiplying in quantity with each cycle
kubejs.ponder.wood_chip_machine.text_3: This simple Wood Chips multiplication line demonstrates how a looping production line operates
kubejs.ponder.wood_chip_machine.text_4: The key to these systems is precisely controlling the ratio of items fed into the loop versus those extracted as output
kubejs.ponder.wood_chip_machine.text_5: You can set a fixed value based on the multiplication rate per cycle...
kubejs.ponder.wood_chip_machine.text_6: ...or use a Brass Tunnel in "Prefer Nearest" mode to prioritize sending items back into the loop over outputting them
kubejs.ponder.wood_chip_machine.text_7: For Wood Chips multiplication, since the multiplication rate exceeds the output rate of a Brass Funnel, you can simply output them directly!
kubejs.ponder.set_redstone_radar.text_1: To establish a Sculk Transmitter communication network, you first need to hold the Sculk Transmitter and right-click on a location to bind the target.
kubejs.ponder.set_redstone_radar.text_2: Right-click another location to place the Sculk Transmitter A bound to the target location.
kubejs.ponder.set_redstone_radar.text_3: Next, place a Sculk Transmitter B at the bound target location as well.
kubejs.ponder.set_redstone_radar.text_4: If you don't need to bind a target for B, you can place a signal-receiving-only transmitter B while sneaking.
kubejs.ponder.set_redstone_radar.text_5: Right-click the top of a Sculk Transmitter with a Wrench toggles whether it loads its chunk.
kubejs.ponder.set_redstone_radar.text_6: Right-click the corresponding side of a Sculk Transmitter with a Wrench can switch its input/output state.
kubejs.ponder.set_redstone_radar.text_7: By doing so, you have established a one-way signal connection from transmitter A to transmitter B!
kubejs.ponder.set_redstone_radar.text_8: If you need to change the bound target of the transmitter, you can right-click it with a Position Data!
kubejs.ponder.superheated_steam_generato: Fill the Steam Generator with Overheated Steam
Besides pressurized steam, steam generators can also use overheated steam to work with the Covariant Reactor for power generation!
Similarly, you need to supply Overheated Steam within a 3x3 area around the generator and provide 25mB of Lube Oil per recipe for the generator
However, unlike the pressurized steam recipe, overheated steam is completely consumed and provides 12,000 FE/t per block of power
Besides that, Overheated Steam power generation is not affected by Water!
kubejs.ponder.use_electrolytic_cell.text: When this happens, you need to reinstall new electrode. A Deployer can also perform this for you
Without disturbing the required structure, you can freely build other stuffs around it
kubejs.ponder.use_infinity_fetching_pool: At this moment, the controller will produce fluid at an extremely high rate (typically 16 B/tick)...
...and output the generated fluid to the 4 containers in the structure at a rate of 20B / 5 ticks each!
